goal: Create scripts/factory/ledger.mjs — the factory subsystem's SQLite WAL run mirror — plus its two test files, per RATIFIED ADR-024 v2 (do not re-litigate the design). The module is a dual-write run recorder: every public writer appends one JSON line to an append-only JSONL raw record FIRST, then mirrors the same normalized arguments into a SQLite database (node:sqlite DatabaseSync, WAL). The JSONL is the authority; the db is a queryable MIRROR that may fail without ever propagating an error to the caller. It never prunes: no row-removal, table-removal or space-reclaiming SQL verb appears anywhere in the file. Also: two new test files, three narrow doc/version touches. Clean-room re-authoring — no GitHub-visible artifact (commit message, PR body, code comment) may name any external project.

EVERY writer follows this exact order:
1. VALIDATE (before the floor branch, so refusals are identical above and below floor): required fields present, enum membership, `type` in `EVENT_TYPES`, an explicit named refusal when `type === 'heartbeat'`. Refusals THROW LedgerUsageError.
2. NORMALIZE: fill defaults (timestamps via `isoMs(now())`, `seq` via the allocator below), apply the payload allowlist and the redaction pass, coerce booleans/undefined. The result is `args` — the fully-resolved argument object.
3. APPEND JSONL: one line `{ v: 1, kind: '<writer method name>', at: isoMs(now()), args }` + '\n' via `appendFileSync`. THIS MAY THROW and the throw PROPAGATES (the raw record is the authority; if we cannot record it, the caller must know).
4. MIRROR: run the INSERT/UPDATE inside `try { … } catch (err) { mirrorErrors += 1; if (!firstCode) firstCode = err.code ?? err.name }`. NEVER rethrow. A lazy-open failure counts here too (the handle then behaves as a no-op mirror for the rest of its life; readers return empty).
CRITICAL replay invariant: NO column is ever derived from the JSONL line's `at` field — every column value comes from `args`. That is precisely what makes replay row-identical despite the replayed line carrying a fresh `at`.

`seq` allocation: `seq` is OPTIONAL on `recordEvent`/`startPhase`/`recordSourceError`. When absent, resolve it from an in-process per-(adw_id, kind) counter seeded on first use from `SELECT MAX(seq) …` (0 when degraded), and write the RESOLVED value into `args` — so the JSONL always carries an explicit seq and replay is deterministic.

`replayJsonl`: read the file, parse each line, refuse (throw) on an unknown `kind` not in `WRITERS`, and dispatch `ledger[line.kind](line.args)` in file order. There is no separate replay code path — this is a dispatcher over the public API, which is the whole point of AC-5.

== 5. FIELD HYGIENE + REDACTION (AC-9) ==
`PAYLOAD_KEYS[type]` is a closed per-event-type key allowlist. Any key not listed is DROPPED and counted (`stats().dropped_payload_keys`), never stored, never logged with its value. Ratified sets: `gate_pass`/`gate_fail` = ['attempt','checks','violations']; `decision` = ['decided','why','alternatives']; `error` = ['reason','source_path','source_kind','byte_size','violation_names'] (this is what `recordSourceError` writes). The remaining seven are backend-lead-authored (see the assumptions block in this spec's return channel): `phase_start` = ['name']; `phase_end` = ['name','status']; `agent_start` = ['role','model','dispatch_id']; `agent_end` = ['role','outcome','dispatch_id']; `tool_call` = ['tool','ok']; `handoff` = ['from_role','to_role','task_id']; `log` = ['level','message'].
Redaction, applied to every writer's args before serialization (i.e. before BOTH the JSONL line and the db bind): drop any key matching `/^DEVTEAM_/i`, and drop any string value containing a secret marker. The marker set is `[NONCE_PREFIX]`, imported from `scripts/cmux/contract.mjs` (its value is the literal `devteam-done-`). Count drops in `stats().redacted_values`. Scan recursively through nested plain objects and arrays.
Why `NONCE_PREFIX` and not a hardcoded string: `contract.mjs` owns it, the cmux subsystem already enforces its absence from records via `assertNoNonce` (record.mjs:164-176), and importing keeps one source of truth. Import it; do not copy the literal.

== 6. recordSourceError — THE VALUE-LEAK CHANNEL ==
`recordSourceError({ adw_id, source_path, source_kind, byte_size, violation_names, reason, seq? })` writes an `error` EVENT row and NO mirror row for the offending source. Two hard rules:
- `violation_names` is built by the CALLER as `violations.map(v => `${v.path}:${v.keyword}`)` — NEVER `v.message`. Reason, verified in source: `scripts/cmux/contract.mjs:157-213` builds every violation's `message` by EMBEDDING the offending value, e.g. `contract.mjs:157`:
```
violations.push({ path, keyword: 'type', message: `expected type ${types.join('|')}, got ${JSON.stringify(value)}` })
```
so a message string is an uncontrolled copy of task-controlled bytes. Document this at the parameter site. Defense in depth: if any element of `violation_names` fails a shape check (a closed pattern of `path:keyword`, no whitespace, bounded length), drop it and count it rather than storing it.
- `reason` comes from `err.name` and is constrained to a CLOSED set: `RecordInvalidError` (the class is exported from scripts/cmux/record.mjs:50 — reference it by name only, do NOT import record.mjs), `SyntaxError`, `Error`. Anything else is coerced to `Error`.
- `byte_size` comes from the caller's own `stat` — the ledger never stats the source file itself.
- A previously-good row is NEVER retracted by a source error (this follows structurally: nothing in this module removes or overwrites a mirror row on an error path).

== 7. HEARTBEATS ARE COLUMNS ==
`processes.last_heartbeat_at` and `agent_sessions.last_heartbeat_at` are updated in place — O(1) rows, no row growth. ONE public method: `heartbeat({ adw_id, target, at, pid, started_at, claude_session_id })` where `target` is `'process'` or `'agent_session'`; it refuses if the natural key for the chosen target is absent (process: adw_id+pid+started_at; agent_session: adw_id+claude_session_id). This single-method shape is what yields ADR-024's `heartbeat` JSONL line kind directly. Heartbeat lines DO go to the JSONL so the raw record stays complete. `heartbeat` is NOT in `EVENT_TYPES` and `recordEvent({type:'heartbeat'})` refuses (AC-2). THE LEDGER OWNS NO TIMER — it never calls setInterval/setTimeout; the caller drives every heartbeat.

== 8. KILL HELPERS (operator-invoked CLI only) ==
Exposed ONLY through the `kill` CLI verb (`--adw-id <id> --pid <n> --yes`), never as a convenience library export used by #41. Gate order: parse/require all three flags -> pid > 1 -> pid !== process.pid -> pid !== process.ppid -> a `processes` row exists for (adw_id, pid) -> the recorded `command` equals the live `ps -p <pid> -o command=` output. Then SIGTERM; poll liveness with `process.kill(pid, 0)` in short slices up to `TERM_TO_KILL_MS`; if still alive, RE-CHECK pid liveness + the ps command + the row's recorded `started_at`, and ABANDON (exit 2, explain) on any mismatch; only then SIGKILL.
Gotchas: use `spawnSync('ps', ['-ww','-p', String(pid), '-o','command='], {encoding:'utf8'})` and `.trim()` the output — verify on your machine that a long argv round-trips without truncation, and drop `-ww` only if it is rejected. A zero-status ps with empty output means the process is gone -> refuse, do not kill. For the synchronous wait use `Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, sliceMs)` in ~100ms slices — note in a comment (per backend-notes.md 2026-08-02) that node cannot dispatch signal handlers while the main thread is blocked synchronously; that is acceptable here because this is a foreground operator command, and it is exactly why the FINALIZER must not share this code path.
Document in-code, at the gate: this is a REFUSAL GATE, NOT identity proof — a pid can be recycled and a command line can be forged; the gate exists to stop the obvious mistake, not to prove identity.

== 9. FINALIZER ==
`installFinalizer({ adw_id, signals = ['SIGTERM','SIGINT'] })` — installed ONLY by this explicit call, NEVER at import. Idempotent: a second call installs nothing and returns the same uninstall handle. On signal: land the open session as `fail`, close every `processes` row still in state `running` (set `ended_at` and state `killed`), set `process.exitCode = 128 + signum` (SIGTERM 143, SIGINT 130), remove its own listener, then re-raise via `process.kill(process.pid, sig)` so the signal is not swallowed (setting exitCode first means a process kept alive by another listener still exits with the right code). It must be structurally distinct from the kill helpers — no shared timing/ps code.
Testing it: write a tiny inline child program via `spawnSync(process.execPath, ['-e', '<program>'])`? No — you need to signal it while it runs, so use `spawn` (async test) with the child opening a ledger at a temp dbPath, installing the finalizer, and idling on a long timer; send SIGTERM; await 'exit'; assert the child's exit signal and then open the db from the test and assert session status `fail` and no `running` process rows. Always kill the child in `after()` with `{force:true}`-equivalent cleanup so a failing test cannot leak a process.

== 10. CLI VERBS ==
`main(argv)` dispatches SIX verbs. Four are READ-ONLY and their spellings are a contract with do-40-02's npm recipes (ORCHESTRATOR-RECONCILED per the ratified package — do not rename): `sessions`, `phases <adw_id>`, `tail <adw_id> [--after <rowid>] [--limit <n>]`, `procs <adw_id>`. `phases`/`tail`/`procs` refuse (exit 2) without an adw_id; `phases` prints the phases rows for that adw_id, `tail` wraps listEvents({adw_id, afterRowid, limit}) (default afterRowid 0, default limit 50), `procs` prints the processes rows — each emits JSON on stdout plus one human line on stderr. DEVOPS CONSULT ANSWERED: do-40-02 lands the matrix as exactly `node-version: ["20", "24"]` (quoted strings, bracketed list, key spelled node-version) — AC-8(f)'s regex targets that shape. Verb detail: `sessions` (JSON on stdout: `{ schema: 1, ledger_version, db_path, degraded, mirror_errors, mirror_first_code, dropped_payload_keys, redacted_values, unverified: [...], sessions: [...] }`, plus a one-line human summary on stderr); `doctor` (prints node version, NODE_FLOOR, degraded state, db path, per-table row counts, the three pragma readbacks, and the FTS5 probe result — printed, never asserted; always exit 0 unless usage error); `kill` (§8). Unknown verb / missing arg -> `refuse(...)` -> exit 2. Below floor, EVERY verb exits 2 with a message naming both `NODE_FLOOR` and `process.versions.node`.
CLI-only test seam for the floor path: the CLI reads `process.env.DEVTEAM_LEDGER_FAKE_NODE_VERSION` (when set) in place of `process.versions.node` for the floor comparison, so AC-8(a) is testable on a Node 24 machine. Document it in-code as a TEST SEAM whose only possible effect is to DEGRADE (it can never bypass the floor: forcing a high version on a low runtime makes the sqlite load fail, which degrades anyway per §3).

interface_contract:
AUTHORITATIVE — backend owns this shape; issue #41 consumes it and must not redefine it.

--- A. Public module surface (scripts/factory/ledger.mjs) ---
Constants (frozen, exported): LEDGER_VERSION=1 · NODE_FLOOR='24.0.0' · TERM_TO_KILL_MS=5000 · TABLES · EVENT_TYPES · PAYLOAD_KEYS · SESSION_STATUSES · PHASE_STATUSES · PROCESS_STATES · WRITERS.
Functions (exported): openLedger({dbPath, jsonlPath?, nodeVersion?, now?, stderr?}) -> Ledger (synchronous, lazy) · defaultDbPath() -> string (CLI only) · replayJsonl(jsonlPath, ledger) -> {applied, skipped} · isoMs(t) -> string · main(argv) -> exitCode.
Ledger handle:
  writers: startSession({adw_id, repo_slug, task_slug, started_at?}) · endSession({adw_id, ended_at?, status, billed_input_tokens?, billed_output_tokens?, billed_cache_write_tokens?, billed_cache_read_tokens?, billed_cost_usd?}) · startPhase({adw_id, seq?, name, started_at?}) -> phase_id · endPhase({adw_id, seq, ended_at?, status}) · recordEvent({adw_id, seq?, type, phase_id?, parent_id?, started_at?, ended_at?, payload?}) · recordEnvelope({adw_id, dispatch_id, slice_id, attempt, role, produced_at, schema_version, envelope_path, body_kind, valid, violation_names}) · recordGateResult({adw_id, phase_id, gate_name, attempt, ok, checks, violations, created_at?}) · startProcess({adw_id, dispatch_id, pid, command, started_at?}) · endProcess({adw_id, pid, started_at, ended_at?, exit_code, exit_signal, state}) · heartbeat({adw_id, target:'process'|'agent_session', at?, pid?, started_at?, claude_session_id?}) · startAgentSession({adw_id, dispatch_id, role, model, claude_session_id, transcript_path, started_at?}) · endAgentSession({adw_id, claude_session_id, ended_at?, context_tokens, context_window, raw_read_tokens, raw_written_tokens, billed_input_tokens, billed_output_tokens, billed_cache_write_tokens, billed_cache_read_tokens}) · recordSourceError({adw_id, source_path, source_kind, byte_size, violation_names, reason, seq?})
  readers: listSessions() · getSession(adw_id) · listEvents({adw_id, afterRowid=0, limit}) · dumpTable(name)
  meta: degraded:boolean · stats() -> {degraded, mirror_errors, mirror_first_code, dropped_payload_keys, redacted_values} · close() · installFinalizer({adw_id, signals?})
Every writer: validate -> normalize -> append JSONL (may throw) -> mirror to db (never throws). No column is ever derived from the JSONL line's `at`.
JSONL line: {v:1, kind:<writer method name, member of WRITERS>, at:<ms-ISO>, args:<fully normalized argument object>}.
CLI: `sessions` | `phases <adw_id>` | `tail <adw_id> [--after <rowid>] [--limit <n>]` | `procs <adw_id>` | `doctor` | `kill --adw-id <id> --pid <n> --yes`. The four read verbs are exactly what package.json's ledger:* recipes invoke (do-40-02 contract; neither side renames alone). Exit 0 ok / 1 unexpected internal error / 2 usage, refusal, or below floor.

--- B. The seven tables (RATIFIED — column names, keys and enums ARE the contract; SQL types are the coder's choice within TEXT/INTEGER/REAL; every timestamp is millisecond-ISO) ---
sessions: adw_id (PK), repo_slug, task_slug, started_at, ended_at, status, billed_input_tokens, billed_output_tokens, billed_cache_write_tokens, billed_cache_read_tokens, billed_cost_usd, ledger_version
phases: id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY), adw_id, seq, name, started_at, ended_at, status — UNIQUE(adw_id, seq)
events: id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT), adw_id, seq, type, phase_id, parent_id, started_at, ended_at, payload_json — UNIQUE(adw_id, seq); INDEX events_adw_id_idx ON events(adw_id, id)
envelopes: id, adw_id, dispatch_id, slice_id, attempt, role, produced_at, schema_version, envelope_path, body_kind, valid, violation_names — UNIQUE(dispatch_id)
gate_results: id, adw_id, phase_id, gate_name, attempt, ok, checks_json, violations_json, created_at — UNIQUE(adw_id, gate_name, attempt)
processes: id, adw_id, dispatch_id, pid, command, started_at, ended_at, exit_code, exit_signal, last_heartbeat_at, state — UNIQUE(adw_id, pid, started_at)
agent_sessions: id, adw_id, dispatch_id, role, model, claude_session_id, transcript_path, started_at, ended_at, context_tokens, context_window, raw_read_tokens, raw_written_tokens, billed_input_tokens, billed_output_tokens, billed_cache_write_tokens, billed_cache_read_tokens, last_heartbeat_at — UNIQUE(adw_id, claude_session_id)
Every insert is INSERT OR IGNORE on the natural key above.

--- C. Enums (closed) ---
EVENT_TYPES (exactly 11): phase_start, phase_end, agent_start, agent_end, tool_call, handoff, gate_pass, gate_fail, decision, log, error. `tool_call` is the ONLY time-spanning type (fills both started_at and ended_at); every other type leaves ended_at null. `heartbeat` is NOT an event type and writing it as one REFUSES.
sessions.status: running | ok | fail | aborted
phases.status: running | ok | fail | skipped
processes.state: running | exited | killed | unknown

--- D. payload_json ---
Stored only under the per-event-type closed key allowlist PAYLOAD_KEYS[type]; unrecognized keys are dropped and counted, never stored. Ratified sets: gate_pass/gate_fail = {attempt, checks, violations}; decision = {decided, why, alternatives}; error = {reason, source_path, source_kind, byte_size, violation_names}. gate_results.checks_json is a JSON array of {item, ok, note} stored VERBATIM — it is #28's gates-CLI vocabulary and is never re-shaped.

--- E. Spend vs occupancy ---
Spend: billed_input_tokens, billed_output_tokens, billed_cache_write_tokens, billed_cache_read_tokens, billed_cost_usd (as named, on sessions and agent_sessions).
Occupancy (agent_sessions only): context_tokens, context_window.
Raw: raw_read_tokens = input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens; raw_written_tokens = output_tokens; cache_read_input_tokens is EXCLUDED from raw and counted only in billed.
Any usage aggregation de-duplicates by message.id, last-occurrence-in-file-order wins — exactly as scripts/task-cost-log.mjs:139-159.

--- F. Environment contract ---
DEVTEAM_LEDGER_DB (full db path override) and DEVTEAM_LEDGER_DIR (ledger directory override) are read ONLY by defaultDbPath(), i.e. only on the CLI path. DEVTEAM_LEDGER_FAKE_NODE_VERSION is a documented CLI-only test seam for the floor check whose only possible effect is degradation. DEVTEAM_LEDGER_TERM_TO_KILL_MS is a documented CLI-only TEST SEAM for the kill verb, parse-validated and clamped to (0, TERM_TO_KILL_MS] — it can only SHORTEN the TERM-to-KILL wait, never lengthen it or bypass a gate (contract amendment, orchestrator, 2026-08-08 — flagged for #41). Ledger directory mode 0700; ledger.db, its -wal/-shm siblings, and ledger.jsonl mode 0600.
